name: AZD9550
lead: AZD9550 is an investigational dual agonist of the glucagon (GCG) and GLP-1 receptors from AstraZeneca, given by subcutaneous injection and studied for obesity, weight-related conditions and liver disease. [1][2][3] The appearance link is body composition: GLP-1-class drugs are being developed to lower body weight and fat mass, and adding glucagon-receptor activity is intended to increase energy expenditure and liver fat handling alongside the appetite effect of GLP-1.

The programme is at an early-to-mid clinical stage. A first-in-human single-ascending-dose study began in 2023, a phase 1/2 multiple-ascending-dose study tests AZD9550 alone and with AZD6234, a selective amylin receptor agonist, and a phase IIb study of the combination against placebo has reported its registry status as completed. [1][2][3] No trial results have been published.
AZD9550 is not approved anywhere and is not available as a prescription product.

paras: The registry describes AZD9550 as a dual glucagon (GCG) and GLP-1 receptor agonist. GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce appetite and slow gastric emptying, while glucagon receptor activation is being explored for its effects on energy expenditure and liver metabolism. [2] AZD6234 is described in the registry as a selective amylin receptor agonist (SARA) and is co-administered with AZD9550 in the combination studies. [2][3]
A single-ascending-dose phase 1 trial in healthy participants (48 participants, started May 2023) was registered under a non-alcoholic steatohepatitis condition. [1]

A phase 1/2 randomised, single-blind, placebo-controlled multiple-ascending-dose study (NCT06151964) started in September 2023 and enrols 166 participants with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes. It has several parts: AZD9550 alone, a part in Japan, a part combining AZD9550 with AZD6234 in people with type 2 diabetes, and a part in people with obesity without diabetes. Parts run roughly 103 to 261 days. Primary outcomes are adverse events, vital signs, ECG and laboratory changes, and pharmacokinetics of repeated weekly doses; primary completion is estimated for January 2027. [2]

The phase IIb ASCEND study (NCT06862791) is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with obesity or overweight and a weight-related comorbidity. It has nine arms: seven combinations of AZD9550 and AZD6234 at different doses and two monotherapy arms, all given as weekly subcutaneous injections against matched placebo. It enrolled 377 participants, started in February 2025, and lists a 36-week primary endpoint of percent change in body weight and the proportion losing at least 5 percent of body weight. The registry shows the study as completed in May 2026. [3]

Other registered studies cover hepatic impairment, formulation bioavailability, oral contraceptive interaction and a platform study in Chinese participants. [4][5][6][7] No results have been published for any of these trials.

card.summary: AstraZeneca's experimental GLP-1/glucagon injection, tested alone and with an amylin agonist, with no published results yet.
card.note: Investigational; no published trial results found.

quick.overview:
AZD9550 is an experimental injectable drug that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, developed by AstraZeneca for obesity.

It has been through phase 1 and phase 2 trials, including a combination with AZD6234, but no results have been published.
quick.mechanism: GLP-1 activation reduces appetite, while glucagon receptor activation is intended to add effects on energy use and the liver. This is as described by the compound class; no AZD9550-specific data are public.
quick.risks: No published safety data were found. It is not approved and is only available in clinical trials.

chain: Reduced appetite and higher energy expenditure (intended)
Lower body weight and liver fat
angle.text: AZD9550 is being tested in people with overweight or obesity as an injectable weight-loss candidate, alone and combined with an amylin-receptor drug. It is investigational and its effects on weight have not been published.
